argument: Dimension 6, ruled directly: the suspended purge does not proceed as written, and nothing is removed from the weapon table. The 17 rows at 15:172-188 survive, because the chapter's own framing sentence already declares what the table is. 15:15 says the tables enumerate weapons keyed to required Disciplines, armor keyed by weight class and slot count, and adventure gear keyed to utility, and that 'Gear is not bought.' A purge ordered against a named possession catalogue is aimed at an artefact this book never shipped; the second column of that table is the gate Coalition B is making live, so deleting the rows deletes the pin. The rows change shape in one respect only: the table stops being a description of objects and becomes the entry-gate column plus the card-facing property bundle, which is why the named-object framing in the reference chapter has to go rather than the weapon table. The purge therefore lands as three editorial artifacts instead of a deletion, and all three sit inside the suspension's scope. First, delete the 17-row duplicate at 22:367-393. It reprints the same 17 weapons under a second header, [Weapon], [Disciplines], [Properties], [Range] against the canonical [Disciplines Required], and its Range column prints Melee on the rows the canonical table leaves blank and appends (thrown) to four more, so 14 of those 17 rows disagree with the law they duplicate. Second, fold the property mapping to one statement. The weapon-to-property map is printed three times: the table column at 15:171, the seven bullets at 15:213-219, and again in the callout at 15:206, which restates the mapping in prose, Longsword to 2 Blades and Greatsword to 2 Blades plus 1 Heavy Weapon. One statement survives; the bullets fold into the Properties cell. Third, repair the armour pointer: 15:245 promises a full table carrying a Stealth column and points at @sec-chapter-armor-shields, while 16:37 prints Armor, Class, DR, Slots and Notes, so either the column or the promise goes. What the equipment chapter becomes. 15 keeps its structure and loses its possession framing: Kits, the Four Lines, Packs, Granted Kits, Re-Kitting at a Town, and Class Recommendations, Weapons, Armour, Mounts and Vehicles. What changes is its authority. It becomes the single source of the entry gate, so the recipe column is the law and no second chapter restates it, and its armour table stops being a partial restatement abroad because the pointer it already carries becomes true. The mount and vehicle rules at 15:324-429 are untouched by Coalition B. Nothing in this architecture reaches them, which is the blast-radius test, and the charge, dismount and vehicle-damage rules keep their home. Blast radius, priced by derivation rather than estimate: 3 rule lines and 1 pointer changed, 9 kit lines reworded, 1 table of 17 rows deleted from the reference chapter, 7 property bullets folded into an existing column, 1 callout folded, 0 ability cards re-keyed, 0 tags added, 0 weapon rows deleted, 0 mount or vehicle lines touched, 1 page reclaimed. Strongest counter-argument, because a solution with no stated risk is an advertisement: making the recipe column live without differentiating the recipes in the same pass converts three strict dominations from harmless flavour into priced gates. Longbow and Shortbow both print 1 Archery and Two-Handed, with triple the range on the Longbow; Spear prints Reach, Thrown and Two-Handed to Halberd's Reach and Two-Handed at the same 1 Polearms; Dagger prints everything Shortsword prints plus Thrown at the same 1 Blades. Model A made live therefore leaves the table worse than the waiver did unless the recipe differentiation ships in the same edit, and the second cost is discontinuity: kits printed under the waiver become conditional retroactively for characters already in play.
